maiasaura:enwiki:10.title: Maiasaura (Maiasaura and the popularisation of the "dinosaur renaissance")

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the Santonian to the Campanian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Santonian – Campanian),

facts.statement: Maiasaura was described by paleontologists Jack Horner and Bob Makela in 1979.
facts.quote: authority: Horner & Makela, 1979

facts.statement: Remains of Maiasaura were discovered in 1978, and the species was formally described in 1979.
facts.quote: Discovered in 1978 during the dinosaur renaissance, the species description of Maiasaura first came in 1979

facts.statement: Whole Maiasaura eggs were discovered in 1979, marking the first complete dinosaur eggs found in North America.
facts.quote: In 1979, one year after the discovery of the nests and juveniles, Maiasaura whole eggs were unearthed, the first discovery of dinosaur whole eggs both on the American continent and in the Western Hemisphere.

facts.statement: Maiasaura has been designated as the official state fossil of Montana.
facts.quote: Maiasaura, whose bones have been found by hundreds in the state of Montana, has been chosen as Montana's state fossil.

facts.statement: Maiasaura reached a maximum length of about 9 meters and a mass of up to 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Maiasaura peeblesorum were large, attaining a maximum known length of about 9 m and an approximate body mass measured at up to 4 MT.

facts.statement: A distinguishing feature of Maiasaura is a prominent, short, solid crest-like structure located between the eyes.
facts.quote: the distinguishing characteristic of Maiasaura peeblesorum is a prominent short, solid crest-like structure situated between the eyes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the eye crest may have been used for headbutting contests between males during breeding season.
facts.quote: This crest may have been used in headbutting contests between males during the breeding season.

facts.statement: Maiasaura were herbivorous and terrestrial dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Maiasaura were herbivorous, terrestrial dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Maiasaura could walk on two legs (bipedally) or four legs (quadrupedally).
facts.quote: They were capable of walking both on two (bipedal) or four (quadrupedal) legs.

facts.statement: It is likely that Maiasaura primarily escaped danger by fleeing in large herds.
facts.quote: It is likely that they primarily resorted to fleeing in the face of danger, using the vast sizes of their herds to be less likely to be targeted.

facts.statement: Mass bone beds in the Two Medicine Formation indicate herds could contain up to 10,000 individuals.
facts.quote: Mass bone beds discovered in the Two Medicine Formation show that herds could be extremely large and comprise as many as 10,000 individuals.

facts.statement: In 1978, paleontologist Bob Makela was contacted by Bill Clemens regarding bones found by a woman in northwestern Montana.
facts.quote: But in 1978 paleontologist Bob Makela had been told by fellow Berkeley paleontologist Bill Clemens that the State of Montana had called him about a north-western Montana woman who had found bones which she wanted to identify.

facts.statement: At the discovery site, Maiasaura bones were visible on the surface without the need for digging.
facts.quote: There, bones were visible on the surface, not even needing to dig.

facts.statement: In July 1979, student Fran Tannenbaum discovered the first whole dinosaur egg in North America under Jack Horner's direction.
facts.quote: The next year in July 1979, during the second summer dig, a lady student named Fran Tannenbaum, under the direction of Jack Horner, discovered the first whole dinosaur egg ever found in North America and in the Western Hemisphere.

facts.statement: It is assumed that a volcanic eruption in the nearby Elkhorn mountains caused the rapid preservation of Maiasaura fossils.
facts.quote: It is assumed that such event was the eruption of a volcano located among the nearby Elkhorn mountains.

facts.statement: Maiasaura peeblesorum is classified within the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Maiasaura peeblesorum is in the tribe Brachylophosaurini along with these related taxa:

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived in herds and raised its young in nesting colonies.
facts.quote: Maiasaura lived in herds and it raised its young in nesting colonies.

facts.statement: Nests in Maiasaura colonies were packed closely together with gaps of around 7 meters, which is less than the length of an adult animal.
facts.quote: The nests in the colonies were packed closely together, like those of modern seabirds, with the gap between the nests being around 7 m; less than the length of the adult animal.

facts.statement: Maiasaura nests were made of earth and contained between 30 and 40 eggs arranged in a circular or spiral pattern.
facts.quote: The nests were made of earth and contained 30 to 40 eggs laid in a circular or spiral pattern.

facts.statement: Fossilized Maiasaura peeblesorum eggs are black with high, prominent ridges on their outer surface.
facts.quote: Fossilized M. peeblesorum eggs are black in color and have high, prominent ridges on the outer surface.

facts.statement: Maiasaura eggs were incubated by heat from rotting vegetation placed in the nest by parents, rather than by parental brooding.
facts.quote: The eggs were incubated by the heat resulting from rotting vegetation placed into the nest by the parents, rather than a parent sitting on the nest.

facts.statement: Hatchling Maiasaura had undeveloped legs and were incapable of walking immediately after hatching.
facts.quote: Upon hatching, fossils of baby Maiasaura show that their legs were not fully developed and thus they were incapable of walking.

facts.statement: Worn teeth on Maiasaura hatchling fossils indicate that adults brought food to the nest.
facts.quote: Fossils also show that their teeth were partly worn, which means that the adults brought food to the nest.

facts.statement: Maiasaura hatchlings grew from 16 to 58 inches in length during their first year.
facts.quote: The hatchlings grew from a size of 16 to 58 in long in the span of their first year.

facts.statement: Research suggests infant Maiasaura were altricial and left the nest after 40 to 75 days.
facts.quote: Based on metabolic growth rates and age estimations of juvenile specimens both in and outside the nests, it is suggested that infant Maiasaura were altricial and left the confines of their nests after 40-75 days (or roughly a little over 1-2 months old).

facts.statement: The mortality rate for Maiasaura dropped to 12.7% for those surviving their second year.
facts.quote: If the animals survived their second year, their mortality rate would drop to 12.7%.

facts.statement: Maiasaura reached sexual maturity in their third year and skeletal maturity at eight years of age.
facts.quote: Sexual maturity was found to occur in their third year, while skeletal maturity was attained at eight years of age.

facts.statement: Maiasaura included rotting wood in its diet and lived in an environment with a long, dry season prone to drought.
facts.quote: It was also found that Maiasaura also included rotting wood in its diet, as well that its environment had a long, dry season prone to drought.

facts.statement: Maiasaura's diet implies it was both a browser and a grazer.
facts.quote: This would imply that Maiasaura was both a browser and a grazer.

facts.statement: Dental wear analysis shows juvenile Maiasaura peeblesorum had more crush wear than adults, who had more shear wear.
facts.quote: Analysis of its dental wear patterns show that juvenile M. peeblesorum exhibited more crush wear than adults, which displayed more shear wear than juveniles.

facts.statement: Dental wear suggests adults fed on tough vegetation while juveniles fed on hard objects like nuts, seeds, or berries.
facts.quote: This suggests that adults fed more on tough, fibrous vegetation while juveniles fed more on hard, brittle objects like nuts, seeds, or berries.

facts.statement: Studies by Saitta et al. suggest one sex of Maiasaura was roughly 45% larger than the other based on size statistics.
facts.quote: Studies of Maiasaura by Saitta et al., suggest that one sex was roughly 45% larger than the other according to the mathematical analysis known as size statistics.

facts.statement: It is currently unknown whether the larger sex of Maiasaura was male or female.
facts.quote: However, it cannot be ascertained at this time whether the larger sex was male or female.

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived alongside troodontids, the basal ornithopod Orodromeus, the dromaeosaurid Bambiraptor, and the tyrannosaur Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: Maiasaura lived alongside the troodontids Stenonychosaurus and Troodon and the basal ornithopod Orodromeus, as well as the dromaeosaurid Bambiraptor and the tyrannosaur Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: In the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Maiasaura lived alongside various ceratopsians, dromaeosaurids, the tyrannosaurid Daspletosaurus, thescelosaurids, pachycephalosaurs, ornithomimids, hadrosaurids, and the ankylosaurid Scolosaurus.
facts.quote: In the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Maiasaura lived alongside the ceratopsians Albertaceratops, Anchiceratops, Chasmosaurus, Coronosaurus, and Wendiceratops, as well as the dromaeosaurids Dromaeosaurus, Saurornitholestes, and Hesperonychus, the tyrannosaurid Daspletosaurus, the orodromine thescelosaurid Albertadromeus, the pachycephalosaurs Foraminacephale and Hanssuesia, the ornithomimid Struthiomimus, the other hadrosaurids Brachylophosaurus, Corythosaurus, and Parasaurolophus, and the ankylosaurid Scolosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Maiasaura was named by Horner and Makela in 1979.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Horner & Makela, 1979

facts.statement: The species Maiasaura peeblesorum was named by Horner and Makela in 1979.
facts.quote: species_authority: Horner & Makela, 1979

facts.statement: Maiasaura peeblesorum is the only known species in the extinct genus Maiasaura.
facts.quote: Maiasaura peeblesorum es la única especie conocida del género extinto Maiasaura

facts.statement: The genus name Maiasaura means 'good mother lizard' in Greek.
facts.quote: del griego «lagarto buena madre»

facts.statement: Maiasaura measured around 9 meters in length and weighed nearly 3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Maiasaura medía alrededor de 9 metros de longitud con un peso de casi 3 toneladas

facts.statement: Maiasaura had a flat beak typical of hadrosaurs and thick noses.
facts.quote: Tenían un pico plano típico de los hadrosáuridos y narices gruesas

facts.statement: Maiasaura had a small sharp crest in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: Tenían una pequeña cresta puntiaguda frente a los ojos

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the eye crest may have been used in head-butting contests between males during the breeding season.
facts.quote: Esta cresta puede haber sido utilizada en concursos de cabezazos entre machos durante la temporada de reproducción

facts.statement: Maiasaura was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Maiasaura era herbívoro

facts.statement: Studies of healed bone stress patterns show that juveniles under 4 years old walked mainly bipedally, switching to a mainly quadrupedal style as they grew.
facts.quote: Los estudios de los patrones de estrés de los huesos curados muestran que los jóvenes menores de 4 años caminaban principalmente bípedos, cambiando a un estilo de caminar principalmente cuadrúpedo cuando crecieron

facts.statement: Maiasaura appeared to have no defense against predators except perhaps its heavy muscular tail and herd behavior.
facts.quote: Parecían no tener defensa contra los depredadores, excepto, quizás, su pesada cola muscular y su comportamiento de rebaño

facts.statement: Maiasaura herds were extremely large and could have comprised up to 10,000 individuals.
facts.quote: Los rebaños eran extremadamente grandes y podrían haber comprendido hasta 10 000 individuos

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived in an interior habitat.
facts.quote: Maiasaura vivía en un hábitat interior

facts.statement: Maiasaura fed on plants, leaves, fruits, and seeds.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de plantas, hojas, frutas y semillas

facts.statement: An adult Maiasaura had to eat 90 kg of vegetation to maintain good health.
facts.quote: Un adulto tenía que comer 90 kg de vegetales para poder tener buena salud

facts.statement: Nests were very close together, with a space of around 7 meters between them, which is less than the length of an adult.
facts.quote: Los nidos estaban muy cerca uno del otro, como en las aves modernas actuales, con un espacio entre los nidos de alrededor de 7 metros, menos que el largo de un adulto

facts.statement: Maiasaura excavated a hole in the ground 2 meters in diameter with a crater shape.
facts.quote: Maiasaura excavaba en el suelo un hueco de 2 m de diámetro con forma de cráter

facts.statement: These nests were made of earth and each contained between 30 to 40 eggs in a circular or spiral pattern.
facts.quote: Estos nidos estaban hechos de tierra y contenían cada uno entre 30 a 40 huevos en un patrón circular o espiralado

facts.statement: The eggs were approximately the size of ostrich eggs.
facts.quote: Los huevos son de aproximadamente el tamaño de los huevos de un avestruz

facts.statement: The eggs were incubated by the heat from decomposing vegetation placed in the nest by the parents, rather than by a parent sitting on them.
facts.quote: Los huevos fueron incubados por el calor resultante de la vegetación en descomposición puesta en el nido por los padres, en vez de que un padre los empollara sentándose en el nido

facts.statement: The young grew from 41 to 147 centimeters in length within their first year.
facts.quote: Las crías crecían de 41 a 147 centímetros de largo en el plazo de su primer año

facts.statement: At this point, or perhaps after another year, the animal left the nest.
facts.quote: A este punto, o quizás después de otro año, el animal abandonaba el nido

facts.statement: When mating, this ornithopod made a nest where it laid between 18 and 30 eggs and waited until they hatched.
facts.quote: Este ornitópodo cuando se apareaba, después hacia un nido en el que ponía entre 18 y 30 huevos y esperaba hasta que nacieran

facts.statement: During incubation, the babies measured 50 cm in length and had light bones, long and weak limbs, an arched spine, and a U-shaped neck similar to adults.
facts.quote: Durante la incubación, los bebés medían 50 cm de longitud y tenían huesos ligeros, extremidades largas y débiles, columna vertebral arqueada y cuello en forma de U semejante al de los adultos

facts.statement: Small individuals remained in the nest because their weak legs prevented them from running or walking.
facts.quote: Los individuos pequeños permanecían siempre en el nido porque sus patas débiles les impedían correr o caminar

facts.statement: It is probable that parents chewed hard plants to make food easier for their young.
facts.quote: Probablemente los padres masticaban las plantas duras para facilitarles el alimento a sus crías

facts.statement: Dozens of nests were found at the site now called Egg Mountain in Montana, USA.
facts.quote: Junto a los restos descubiertos se encontraron decenas de nidos en el yacimiento hoy en día llamado Egg Mountain (literalmente 'Montaña de los Huevos'), en Montana, Estados Unidos

facts.statement: It was described by paleontologists Jack Horner and Robert Makela as the holotype of a new species.
facts.quote: y descrito por los paleontólogos de dinosaurios Jack Horner y Robert Makela como el holotipo de una nueva especie

facts.statement: The specific name honors the families of John and James Peebles, whose land yielded the findings.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a las familias de John y James Peebles, en cuya tierra se hicieron los hallazgos

facts.statement: The generic name refers to Marion Brandvold's 1978 discovery of a nest with eggshell fragments and babies too large to be hatchlings.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se refiere al descubrimiento de Marion Brandvold en 1978 de un nido con restos de cáscaras de huevo y bebés demasiado grandes para ser crías

facts.statement: More than 200 specimens of all age ranges have been found.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado más de 200 especímenes, de todos los rangos de edad

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived during the late Upper Cretaceous period, approximately 76.7 to 70.6 million years ago, in the Campanian stage in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente entre 76,7 y 70,6 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: Maiasaura is classified as an ornithopod hadrosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido

facts.statement: Recently, Maiasaura was placed in a new clade called Brachylophosaurini along with Brachylophosaurus and Acristavus.
facts.quote: Recientemente, junto con Brachylophosaurus y Acristavus, fue situado en un nuevo clado llamado Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Experts believe Maiasaura lived in enormous nomadic herds that annually returned to the same breeding site due to the large number of nests and skeletons found in North America.
facts.quote: Debido a la gran cantidad de nidos y esqueletos encontrados en Norteamérica, los expertos creen que los maiasaura vivían en enormes manadas nómadas, que anualmente regresaban al mismo lugar de reproducción

facts.statement: It is possible that nests were reused from one year to the next.
facts.quote: Es posible que los nidos fueran reutilizados de un año a otro

facts.statement: Maiasaura was contemporary with Orodromeus, Troodon, the ceratopsid Centrosaurus, the armored Euoplocephalus, and earlier relatives of the tyrannosaur Daspletosaurus and Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: El Maiasauria fue contemporáneo al Orodromeus, Troodon, el ceratópsido Centrosaurus, el macizo Euoplocephalus y parientes más tempranos del tiranosaurio, el Daspletosaurus y Gorgosaurus

facts.statement: These animals were not equipped with powerful weapons to repel predators, so they probably used flight or camouflage as a strategy.
facts.quote: Estos animales no estaban dotados con poderosas armas para repeler a los depredadores, por lo que probablemente utilizaran la huida o el camuflaje como estrategia

facts.statement: This high growth rate can be considered evidence that they possessed warm blood.
facts.quote: Esta alta tasa de crecimiento puede ser considerado como una prueba de que poseían sangre caliente

facts.statement: It is debated whether the crest was used in head-butting contests between males during the breeding season.
facts.quote: Esta cresta puede haber sido utilizada en concursos de cabezazos entre machos durante la temporada de reproducción

facts.statement: It is debated whether the animal left the nest at the end of its first year or perhaps after another year.
facts.quote: A este punto, o quizás después de otro año, el animal abandonaba el nido

facts.statement: Maiasaura chicks remained in the nest for two years.
facts.quote: La cría permanecía en el nido por 2 años.

facts.statement: Maiasaura babies grew very fast, doubling their length in just four weeks.
facts.quote: Los bebés crecían muy rápido, duplicaban su longitud en tan solo cuatro semanas.

facts.statement: Fossils indicate that Maiasaura was ready to leave the nest and join the herd at approximately 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Por medio de fósiles se ha descubierto que cuando alcanzaba aproximadamente 1,5 m de largo ya estaba listo para abandonar el nido y unirse a la manada.

facts.statement: Rapid growth in Maiasaura is considered one of the theories suggesting that dinosaurs were warm-blooded.
facts.quote: de hecho el crecer rápido es una de las teorías por las cuales los dinosaurios son de sangre caliente porque han necesitado alimentarse mucho para crecer de ese modo

facts.statement: Maiasaura reached adulthood between 4 and 6 years of age.
facts.quote: Pero ya llegaba a la edad adulta cuando tenía entre 4 y 6 años.

facts.statement: Maiasaura had short, robust limbs with legs longer than its arms.
facts.quote: Las extremidades eran cortas y robustas y las patas más largas que los brazos.

facts.statement: Female Maiasaura likely returned to the same nesting site every year, sometimes with up to 10,000 other animals.
facts.quote: Al parecer la maiasauria hembra regresaba a anidar cada año al mismo lugar, hasta con 10000 animales más.

facts.statement: Young Maiasaura had to migrate to other forests once they were strong enough to ensure food for the herd.
facts.quote: Cuando los jóvenes eran lo suficientemente fuertes debían migrar a otros bosques para asegurar el alimento de la manada

facts.statement: The genus Maiasaura belongs to the parent group Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Brachylophosaurini

facts.statement: Maiasaura is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Maiasaura belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Maiasaura lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Research by Hunter & Janis (2026) suggests Maiasaura shifted its diet from nutritious, low-fiber plants to nutritionally poor, high-fiber plants as it matured.
facts.quote: Hunter & Janis (2026) compare tooth wear in juvenile and adult individuals of Maiasaura peeblesorum, and report evidence of differences interpreted as consistent with a shift from feeding on nutritious, low-fiber plants to feeding on nutritionally poor, high-fiber plants during the life of the studied dinosaur.
